proof.criterion: A5 / R3 - a queued root adopted by a release while Dispatch shows it blocked waits at admitted and starts when its last blocker closes.

proof.criterion: A6 / R4 - a status write never lands over a change Dispatch recorded after the daemon's read, and the boot corrects an issue whose Dispatch status differs from its phase.
proof.surface: The real Dispatch server process against a scratch database, with the daemon's own outbox writing through its HTTP client (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/status_scratch_dispatch_test.go).
proof.observed: --- PASS: TestTheBootsStatusWriteLandsOnScratchDispatchAfterAnEventOvertakesItsRead (11.28s) and --- PASS: TestABootStatusWriteDoesNotLandOverACloseScratchDispatchTookAfterItsRead (6.51s). proof.criterion: A9 / R7 - a worker that holds its phase with nothing pending is given its phase task within two minutes of ready, for every way a claim comes back, and a holder whose task is still pending gets no second copy.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine and the real outbox runner over a real Postgres claim store, with the runtime's three come-backs driven as the daemon drives them (packages/daemon/internal/daemon/ready_worker_resume_test.go).
proof.observed: --- PASS for all three come-backs in each test: an operator's suspend and resume, a relaunch after a death, and a resume after a pod replacement. The bound is measured where the claim view carries it, the delivery's deliveredAt less the claim's lastReady, and is inside two minutes in each; the task is the phase's resume task for the phase the issue stands in. With a task still pending, no outbox row is written, the delivery id is unchanged, and every prompt carries that one id.

proof.criterion: A8 / R6 - a root architect killed three times in turns fails, a turn that ends normally between the deaths clears the count, the restarted worker's first prompt names the cause, and the state shows each worker's last turn start and end.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine over a real Postgres claim store, driven through the runtime observations a dying pod produces (packages/daemon/internal/supervise/death_cause_test.go).
proof.observed: --- PASS for all five. Three deaths in turns fail the claim; a normal turn end between the second and third clears the count, so the third is the first again; a death with no turn open and nothing pending counts nothing, which is what stops three evictions failing an idle claim; the last death's cause and the last failed start's cause are kept apart rather than overwriting each other; and both, with the claim's last ready time, survive a rebuild from the store.
proof.negativeControl: The tester's run at main: chargeDeath counts only a death with a task pending, so a worker that dies three times mid-turn with nothing pending is restarted for ever and the held and worker-died notices name no cause - dispatch://INFRA-482's architect, which died six times in 54 minutes and was never told why. Recorded in .legion/INFRA-714/test.json.

proof.criterion: A10 / R8 - with the recorded session missing from the store, a suspend and resume brings the claim to ready in a new session, uncharged, and the loss is reported on the issue, to the architect, to the controller and in the new session.
proof.surface: The real supervise machine over a real Postgres, with the runtime answering the missing session as each runtime answers it, and the engine's own reporting path (packages/daemon/internal/supervise/sessionloss_test.go, internal/workflow/session_fault_test.go).
proof.observed: --- PASS for all four. A session no store holds starts the worker fresh, charges nothing, and reports the loss with the lost session's path on the issue, to the architect, to the controller and in the new session's own first prompt. proof.criterion: A12 / R10 - every legion claims command on a worker whose start does not finish answers within its --wait, and a suspend of a starting worker charges no failure.
proof.surface: The shipped legion binary's own command surface against a daemon whose start does not finish (packages/daemon/cmd/legion/claims_wait_test.go), and the real supervise machine for the charge.

Every subcommand answers inside its bound with done, held until when, or a refusal naming its reason; the default is one minute; the bound is on the whole call rather than on one request of it; and a suspend of a starting worker cancels the start and leaves the claim's budgets untouched.

proof.criterion: A14 / R12 - a pass reported after the check's look ended by its bound, by an operator hold or by the implementer's restart closes the check as passed, and a refused report applies when it is sent again.
proof.surface: The daemon's workflow engine and the intake's own fact application over a real Postgres (packages/daemon/internal/workflow/check_late_report_test.go, internal/intake/refused_check_report_test.go).
proof.observed: --- PASS for all three. A report of the current look is recorded however that look ended, and a late pending is recorded as pass and fail are. A refused check report alone leaves its event unmarked, so the same report applies when sent again; every other refused fact stays marked, which is what keeps a refused handoff from becoming retryable.

Recorded in .legion/INFRA-714/test.json. Beside it, the scoping control: TestARefusedFactThatIsNoCheckReportStaysRecorded fails if the un-marking is widened past the CheckReport handler.

packages/daemon gains a changelog: .changie.yaml, CHANGELOG.md, six INFRA-714 fragments, and its line in changelog-fold.yaml's CHANGELOG_PACKAGES.
trickyParts: The harness this change is proven on must be rebuilt in every new pod, because the issue's disk dies with the pod. The recipe is a comment on INFRA-714 and is three steps: Postgres 17 from six Debian .debs unpacked with dpkg-deb -x (postgresql-17, postgresql-client-17 and libpq5 - the client package is where psql and pg_isready live - plus libicu76, without which initdb fails on a loader error, libxslt1.1, and postgresql-17-pgvector 0.8.0-1); liveness by pg_isready on the port and never pg_ctl or postmaster.pid, since each role's container has its own PID namespace; and a local nats-server. pgvector is required: the four scratch-Dispatch rigs boot the real Dispatch server, whose migration 0072_embeddings_core needs the vector extension.

The forward merge with main took two rulings. sjawhar/legion#2478's healing pass re-reads GitHub on a timer, which R1 forbids, so the pass lost and everything of that change not depending on a periodic read was kept: consumer positions whole, legion state's intake lag whole, the delivery-dedupe event ids, the implementer completion read with HANDOFF_NO_PULL_REQUEST, and the pull-request-missing notice, which now has an event-driven producer in the per-issue read. sjawhar/legion#2521 won whole, so nothing here reintroduces a pause at a phase end or in awaiting_person.

HandoffCompleteRequest.Ready is still on the wire and reaches no fact: the plugin posts it on every completion and the body decoder refuses an unknown member. Cutting it is a plugin change for a later release, and the field's own doc says so.

Two forward merges with main were needed, each because GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING and a conflicting head runs no checks at all. The second took three conflicts, all in files this change deletes: dispatch://INFRA-825 had changed internal/ghautomerge on main to fix GitHub's squash message, and this change deletes the daemon's merge entirely and moves that same rule into the merger's own command, so the deletion wins and the fix is not lost. Every proof above was run again at the merge head, which is the head they name.

Round two answered the tester's three defects. tellGateMoved returned the error when it could not build a holder's claim token, which aborted the transaction the gate's own move was written in - so a tree whose root key is not an issue key left the gate closed under the very workers the message exists to warn. A holder that cannot be named is now logged and skipped and the rest are told, which internal/admit's readmission test proves. The carried merger's task no longer names an approved head and one assertion still required it. The plugin's state fixture predated the forward merge and lacked repositories.withoutWebhookApp and consumers, and its pinned tool schema still listed awaiting_merge; both made packages/pi-legion red at the head and the A13 proof false, and 468 TypeScript tests now pass.

The issue's pod was replaced twice during this change, and the second time the round's work was not on GitHub. The merge lane rescued the workspace to a branch as one commit. That commit is a whole merge tree, so its file list mixes this branch's edits with main's and cannot be read as a change set; the way back was to recreate the merge with its true parents and restore the tree from the rescue, not to cherry-pick files. The round therefore lands as one commit carrying a forward merge and the fixes together, which its message says.
deviations: Spec departure 1 of the plan, the merger's approved-head comparison, was declined by the issue's architect on the owner's ruling (dispatch://INFRA-714/ask/beea7685): Legion does not re-implement a repository's rules. The merger keeps one hygiene step, sending a head that still carries .legion/<issue>/ back to retro, and no approved-head comparison was written anywhere.

Decision D2 of the plan, a durable outbox row re-reading the merge state while an approval stands, was declined by the architect. The merge state is read on each event about the pull request, each CI settlement and each push to its base, and the unknown ladder is bounded at five reads thirty seconds apart with nothing standing behind it.

Two reviewer findings were deliberately not applied in the simplify pass: rewriting the base-push fan-out into a join, and moving the merge-state trigger's lookups out of the fact lock. Both are design changes rather than simplifications, and this change is already large. The costs are recorded here so the reviewer can weigh them: the fan-out reads one issue row and rewrites one whole pull-request row per open pull request on a pushed base, and the trigger repeats inside the fact lock the lookups the engine has just made.

A1's main-side run: the tests of R1, R2 and the phase vocabulary cannot compile at main 8a911ecca3a5, because this change deletes the packages and the phase they name - internal/requiredchecks, internal/ghautomerge, the READY route, phase.AwaitingMerge. For those the evidence is a negative control per entry: the production code deliberately broken at this head until the covering test goes red, then reverted. For R3 to R8 and R10 to R12, whose subjects all exist at main, the main-side run is a black-box observation at main, made by this issue's tester and recorded in .legion/INFRA-714/test.json; each entry names the one it rests on. My earlier handoff generalised the impossibility argument from the first set to the second, which was wrong, and the architect corrected it.

The reviewer's critical finding 1 was escalated to the architect as a design decision. I proposed carrying the merge state across a handoff-only push; the architect ruled for dropping the skip-checks trailer from the reviewer's push instead, because GitHub computes mergeStateStatus for the current head alone, so every later read would answer blocked for the trailered head and overwrite anything carried. That ruling is implemented. The head-tying half of my proposal was kept, as the architect directed, since it is the reviewer's finding 4.
openQuestions: The merger's handoff_complete now records its phase row and triggers nothing, since the merge is what moves the issue. So the architect hears nothing between retro's completion and the merge. That follows from R2, which says the merger sends no completion, but it is a real loss of signal; telling the architect would be an addition rather than a deletion and was not made.
discoveredComplexity: cmd/legion's TestProbeImageReadsEachRolesOwnOverlaysAsTheRoleStarts fails in a Kubernetes issue pod on this branch's base as well; it was reproduced at the parent commit with every changed file restored. internal/intake's TestConsumerLagCountsEveryConsumerWhileNATSRefusesTheOldestMessageRead starts a NATS container and internal/runtime/tmux's TestNewRefusesLaunchersItCannotRun wants tmux on PATH, neither of which a pod has, and nine internal/daemon tests are the known gVisor and Docker cases. CI's run at this head is the proof for all of them.

TestTheKeeperRetriesAControllerWhoseLaunchesRanOut was a race rather than a pre-existing failure, which two workers reported it as. Its three refused launches and the keeper's retry all fell between two ten-millisecond polls, so the wait read zero spawns and then four and never the failure it exists to prove. The retry is now two seconds; the test ran five times green.
